case.label: B
case.text: IAM Identity Center is the AWS-recommended path for workforce console access, can use AWS Managed Microsoft AD as its identity source, and assigns permission sets to directory groups, so a candidate who knows 'Identity Center replaces IAM users' picks B. The case fails on the stem's explicit constraints: B names an account instance, and account instances serve application access only, not AWS account access through permission sets; an organization instance would need AWS Organizations, which the company will not adopt. C (AD FS plus SAML roles) also works but adds EC2 servers to run and patch, so LEAST operational overhead rules it out. D (directory access URL plus console access with IAM roles assigned to the directory group) is the native, no-extra-infrastructure answer. Wording check: the stem's 'does not use AWS Organizations' and 'keep this single-account setup' are deliberate constraints rather than cues that name the answer; D omits the explicit step 'enable AWS Management Console access' but 'let them sign in at that URL' implies it, which is not enough to make another option defensible.
